headline: Iran attacks two US-guarded oil tankers in Strait of Hormuz
summary: The attacks occurred while President Donald Trump was meeting with his cabinet to discuss the war and rising fuel prices.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that they attacked and stopped two oil tankers that were under US Navy escort in the Strait of Hormuz.
The IRGC stated that the tankers were using an 'undeclared route' to cross the strait, while four other tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions.
Tensions have escalated as Iran bombs ships using the southern route near the Oman coast, while the US attacks ships violating Iran's imposed blockade.
Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz has nearly stopped since the conflict resumed two weeks ago, causing crude oil prices to surge past $90 per barrel.

In other developments, Kuwait reported intercepting an Iranian drone targeting its military installations, and Israel carried out massive explosions near the Beaufort Castle in Lebanon to destroy Hezbollah tunnels.
President Trump met with his cabinet at Camp David to determine the future of the war, which has now lasted five months despite initial promises that it would end in a few weeks.
The conflict is causing significant inflation in the US, with fuel and essential goods prices rising, which may impact the upcoming midterm elections.
Public support for the war is at its lowest point, with a recent poll showing only one in three Americans support the conflict.
caption:
Iran has attacked two US-guarded oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices soaring above $90 per barrel.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that they attacked and stopped two oil tankers that were under US Navy escort in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC stated that the tankers were using an 'undeclared route' to cross the strait, while four other tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions.

Tensions have escalated as Iran bombs ships using the southern route near the Oman coast, while the US attacks ships violating Iran's imposed blockade.

Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz has nearly stopped since the conflict resumed two weeks ago, causing crude oil prices to surge past $90 per barrel.

In other developments, Kuwait reported intercepting an Iranian drone targeting its military installations, and Israel carried out massive explosions near the Beaufort Castle in Lebanon to destroy Hezbollah tunnels.

President Trump met with his cabinet at Camp David to determine the future of the war, which has now lasted five months despite initial promises that it would end in a few weeks.

The conflict is causing significant inflation in the US, with fuel and essential goods prices rising, which may impact the upcoming midterm elections.

Public support for the war is at its lowest point, with a recent poll showing only one in three Americans support the conflict.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[inspects Dhaka city management]] by driving himself
headline: PM Tarique Rahman inspects Dhaka city management by driving himself
summary: The Prime Minister spent over two hours visiting various areas of Dhaka North City Corporation to identify shortcomings in civic services.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman conducted an on-site inspection of waste management, drainage, and greening services across Dhaka North City Corporation yesterday.
Driving the vehicle himself, the Prime Minister visited numerous locations including Mirpur DOHS, Uttara, Mohakhali, Farmgate, and Banani to assess the ground reality of civic services.
During the tour, he identified several problems and expressed dissatisfaction with various issues, ordering relevant authorities to take immediate corrective action.
The inspection lasted more than two and a half hours, covering key areas such as Airport Road, Kakoli, and the Gono Bhaban intersection.
According to the Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony, the Prime Minister personally inspected the conditions because he wants Dhaka to be a clean city.
He was accompanied by State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam, DNCC Administrator Md Safiqul Islam, and other senior officials.
caption:

During the tour, he identified several problems and expressed dissatisfaction with various issues, ordering relevant authorities to take immediate corrective action.
